newsitem.title: FINLAND: Amer K-owners to not talk anew with Moyne.
newsitem.headline: Amer K-owners to not talk anew with Moyne.

text.p: The Finnish institutions owning K-shares in sporting goods group Amer-Yhtyma Oy said on Thursday they would not reopen talks with British investor Lord Moyne or start talks with anyone else about selling their shares, an Amer spokeswoman told Reuters by telephone.

The three institutions -- the Finnish Association of Graduate Engineers, the Finnish Association of Graduates of the Schools of Economics and Business Administration and the Land and Water Technology Foundation -- said in a statement that their "authorised negotiators were announcing that talks with Lord Moyne will not be started anew."
"The negotiators will not start talks with any other party either," the statement said, but gave no further details.

Jonathan Bryan Guinness, the third Lord Moyne, offered early in June to buy almost 60 percent of votes in Amer for 301 million markka. The K-shareholders initially approved the deal but later pulled out.
Before that cancellation, Norvestia Oy, a Finnish investment company, issued a rivalling bid, which the K-shareholders largely ignored.

Amer's four K-shareholders, bound by an agreement to sell or keep their stakes together, have been eager for a long time to divest their holdings. The K-shares control over 90 percent of votes in Amer.
The fourth K-owner, the Student Union of the Helsinki School of Economics and Business Administration, has kept silent during the latest events.

Finnish radio news reported later on Thursday that the K-shareholders may now go back to an earlier plan to convert their K-shares into bourse-listed A-shares and so be able to sell their stakes each on their own.

A board proposal to this effect had been approved by the four institutions and was about to be endorsed by an extraordinary shareholders' meeting when Lord Moyne's surprise offer emerged. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, news@reuters.fi
